shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
We fear death because we can't imagine non-existence, but we already experienced billions of years of it before we were born and it was fine.
The people who say they're "bad with technology" are usually just people who haven't broken enough things yet.
You only realize how quiet your house is when you're trying to be quiet.
If you've ever felt like you're living someone else's life, you might actually be right—you're just living the version of it that younger you decided on.
The most honest thing about you is probably in your search history, not your diary.
You can't remember most of your life, which means most of you is already gone and you never got a chance to say goodbye to it.
A playlist you loved ten years ago is a time capsule you can actually enter.
The reason meetings could've been emails is the same reason we still have meetings—nobody wants to be alone with their thoughts.
You've probably given the best advice of your life to someone who didn't listen, and taken the worst advice from someone you trusted completely.
Mirrors show you what you look like, but they don't show you how you actually look—because you're always seeing yourself reversed.
The friend who remembers your birthday without a reminder cares about you; the friend who forgets despite a reminder notification might care about you too, they just relate differently to time.
Every "someday" is actually tomorrow being postponed.
You're the most interesting person in the world to yourself and the least interesting to almost everyone else, and both things are true simultaneously.
The reason nostalgia feels so good is because you're remembering the feeling, not the actual experience—you're essentially addicted to your own highlights reel.
Writing a to-do list is just agreeing to disappoint yourself in organized format.
If aliens ever find us, the first thing they'll study is our ability to complain about things we've chosen.
The people who hurt you probably didn't know they were doing it, and the people you hurt probably did, which is why forgiveness is always unfair.
You know you're truly tired when sleeping becomes something you have to schedule.
Death is the only thing that's guaranteed to happen, which might actually make it the most reliable part of life.

motivational.thought:

— Unknown

Success is not final, and failure is not fatal. What matters is the courage to continue.
— Winston Churchill

Your obstacles are not punishments—they're invitations to discover who you really are.
— Unknown

Discipline is remembering what you want more than you want comfort.
— Unknown

— Chinese Proverb

You're not behind. You're not lost. You're exactly where you need to be to become who you're meant to be.
— Unknown

Every expert was once a beginner who refused to quit.
— Unknown

The life you want is on the other side of the work you're avoiding.
— Unknown

Regret for the things we did is temporary. Regret for the things we didn't do is permanent.
— Unknown

Your potential is infinite, but your time is finite. Choose accordingly.
— Unknown

A person who never made a mistake never tried anything new.
— Albert Einstein

The only failure is the failure to try.
— Unknown

What lies behind us and what lies before us are small matters compared to what lies within us.
— Ralph Waldo Emerson

Progress whispers, but regret screams.
— Unknown

The gap between who you are and who you want to be is not a problem—it's a purpose.

Growth happens in the quiet moments when no one is watching.

— Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she was drawing her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.

My therapist asked what my biggest fear is.
I said, "Abandonment." She said, "We'll continue this next week," and I knew I was right.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My friend said he's been sober for a year.
I said, "That's amazing!" He said, "Not really, I just can't afford it anymore."

I went to a wedding last weekend.
Two strangers promised to spend their lives together. I give it five years, tops. The groom looked like he was already serving time.

My doctor told me I need to cut back on alcohol.
I said, "Okay." He said, "I'm serious." I said, "So am I—I'm going to need a second opinion."

I asked my dad why he never says "I love you."
He said, "I show it through my actions." I said, "You left when I was three." He said, "Exactly—I'm saving you money on therapy by doing it myself."

People say money can't buy happiness.
They've clearly never bought a dog. Or euthanized one. Actually, don't do that—that's expensive AND sad.

I tried online dating for three months.
Now I understand why some species eat their young.

My boss asked why I've been so quiet at work lately.
I said, "I'm just trying to give everyone the gift of my absence."

I love when people say, "You look tired."
Thanks for noticing. I've been practicing for my funeral.

My gym trainer said, "No pain, no gain."
I said, "Great, because I'm in constant pain and I haven't gained anything but debt."

I told my kid the tooth fairy isn't real.
He cried for an hour. Then he realized his parents have been stealing from him and he got ANGRY.

My friend asked if I believe in life after death.
I said, "I don't know, but I believe in rent after graduation."

I went to a "live your best life" seminar.
Turns out my best life costs $47 per month plus shipping.

I asked my barber what he recommends for hair loss.
He said, "A different barber."

My mom asked why I'm not married yet.
I said, "Because I like eating, sleeping, and keeping my money." She said, "Those aren't mutually exclusive." I said, "You married Dad."

I told my therapist I feel like nobody listens to me.
She said, "That must be frustrating." I said, "Wait—you do listen?" She said, "I bill by the hour, so yes."

My Uber driver said, "So, what do you do?"
I said, "I'm an existential dread consultant." He said, "For companies?" I said, "No, for myself. Business is good."
I love my job. It gives me something to do during the day so I don't think about my crippling loneliness at night.
